author: reek
body: The depth buffer is indexed by the visible width and the colour buffer by the stride, so a framebuffer whose PixelsPerScanLine exceeds its horizontal resolution is written without shear and its padding is never touched.

author: reek
body: A repainting view builds its target once and clears it per frame. Rebuilding the target instead would allocate a fresh depth buffer every frame, which at panel size is megabytes that never come back.

author: reek
body: A lit surface keeps its own colour: the diffuse term is the albedo times the light, not the light alone. Scaling the bare light colour by the Lambert term, as this did, makes every lit face the colour of the lamp and leaves the material visible only in what ambient contributes, so a blue cube under a white key light comes out white.

author: reek
body: The cone is fully lit at a fragment cosine of `angle` milli or tighter, fades linearly across the `falloff` band below it, and is dark outside.

author: reek
body: A depth-only pass from the first directional light's view fills a map; the main pass carries each vertex's light-space position and compares the interpolation against the map per pixel. A fragment farther from the light than what the light saw is shadowed and answers the ambient-only colour. The transform to light space happens per VERTEX; per pixel there are only the three integer interpolations and one map read, for the same reason nothing else in this chapter allocates per pixel.

author: reek
body: The bias is in depth-buffer units, a 10^6 span across the light frustum: too small and a surface shadows itself in stripes, too large and shadows detach from their casters.

author: reek
body: r3d-render-into renders through a caller-supplied target, which is how a scene reaches a real framebuffer: build one with r3d-target-at from the base and stride the firmware reported. r3d-render-scene keeps the offline shape, converting the flat buffer to a Framebuf once at the end rather than a record per pixel.

author: reek
body: Vec3 is Real, so normalization and reflection are the Matrix4 primitives rather than the fixed-point integer routines this chapter used to carry. r3d-vec-len still answers in world units as an integer, because the point light compares it against an integer radius.
